notes.title: Pump, Flip and Fire Pack DLC | Patch 8.2 | Out Now!
notes.notes: [p]Pump, flip, unfold, and fire with 3 curated tactile hunting weapons: a modern lever-action rifle, a fast-loading pump-action rifle, and a lightweight portable folding shotgun. Available now![/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="E08BjCScFv0;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h1]Pump, Flip and Fire Weapon Pack[/h1][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3750770/theHunter_Call_of_the_Wild__Pump_Flip_and_Fire_Pack/"][/dynamiclink][/p][h2]Anantha Action .22 MAG[/h2][list][*][p]Lightweight and sturdy lever-action rifle.[/p][/*][*][p]Smooth action, low recoil.[/p][/*][*][p]Recommended for small game (Animal Class: 1-2).[/p][/*][*][p]New ammo: hollow point and jacketed hollow point .22 Magnum.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/bad43cfb52942988d1f4c4075b55d064c5c66967.png"][/img][/p][h2]Frost .257[/h2][list][*][p]Classic magazine-fed pump-action rifle.[/p][/*][*][p]Versatile and powerful.[/p][/*][*][p]Recommended for multiple animal classes (2-6).[/p][/*][*][p]New ammo: soft point and polymer tip .257 Roberts ammo.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/7afc373908c4f613d4dec5b524ad27a6c72b1478.png"][/img][/p][h2]Giddings SSC .410 Coyote[/h2][list][*][p]Ultra-lightweight and single-shot folding shotgun.[/p][/*][*][p]Folds for easy backpack storage.[/p][/*][*][p]Ideal for close range and quick shots (Animal Class: 1-5).[/p][/*][*][p]It can be used with .410 birdshot ammo and all new .410 buckshot and slug ammo too.[/p][/*][/list][h1][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/1fd0cb44be7943d5591c3e465d959c87e303eb63.png"][/img][/h1][h1]Patch 8.2[/h1][h2]Highlights[/h2][p]We've completely overhauled the initial hunts on Hirschfelden, Layton Lake District, and Medved-Taiga to be more intuitive for new players. Easier first harvests are now within reach with helpful point-of-interest icons and highlighted organs. [/p][p][/p][p]Plus, keep an eye out for two stunning new Gray Wolf variations (Melanistic Charcoal and Acromelanistic) and a visual upgrade to the lying-down Gray Wolf trophy! [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/dcb638d4571028577fbfb2dcb6c416dd85d385ae.png"][/img][/p][p]We've also remastered the Mule Deer TruRacs, adding a variety of new antler variations, and fixed some bugs.[/p][p][/p][p]Full Patch Notes:[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/518790/view/511841259183145356?l=english"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]Happy hunting![/p]

notes.title: Patch 8.2 Notes
notes.notes: [h1]Pump, Flip and Fire Pack DLC[/h1][p]This weapon pack features three new tactile firearms that bring a fresh level of versatility to your hunts.[/p][list][*][p]Anantha Action .22 MAG - lightweight but sturdy lever-action rifle.[/p][/*][*][p]Frost .257 - a classic magazine-fed pump-action rifle.[/p][/*][*][p]Giddings SSC .410 Coyote - an ultra lightweight single-shot folding shotgun.[/p][/*][/list][previewyoutube="XZsRiKt3n3U;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h1]Patch 8.2[/h1][p]We'll be transitioning to a numbered system (8.2, 8.3, and so on) for future releases. These release numbers won't directly match the build numbers you see in-game.[/p][p]We hope this change will make it easier to discuss and keep track of which patch was when in the future.[/p][p][/p][h2]New Features[/h2][p][b]First Hunt Overhaul[/b][/p][p]New players will find their initial hunts on Hirschfelden, Layton Lake District, and Medved-Taiga to be more intuitive than ever. We've added a helpful point of interest icon and highlighted organs when aiming, making those first harvests easier to achieve.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Rare Gray Wolf Variations[/b][/p][p]Keep your eyes peeled for two brand new Gray Wolf fur variations: Melanistic Charcoal and Acromelanistic.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/36d5a3a094aa625cfb881ad747385c904358620c.png"][/img][/p][h2]Improvements[/h2][list][*][p]We've given the Gray Wolf trophy a visual upgrade when displayed lying down. [/p][/*][*][p]We've addressed issues with the Bighorn Sheep skeletal model in the X-ray view and smoothed out its running animation.[/p][/*][*][p]The Mule Deer TruRacs have been remastered. We also added multiple new antler variations for this species.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Bug Fixes[/h2][p][/p][p][b]Animals[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where the trophy rating for the Male Springbok was capped..[/p][/*][*][p]North American Beaver’s droppings will now be displayed correctly as droppings and not tracks.[/p][/*][*][p]Animals will now appear at the correct distance on the harvest screen when shot while running.[/p][/*][*][p]Beaver mating calls will display visual waves and trigger interactions when the animal is in the water.[/p][/*][*][p]Pheasant hens will no longer have a line on their wings in the harvest screen.[/p][/*][*][p]Beavers’ skinning on the tail has been improved, and liver shots will display correctly in the X-ray model.[/p][/*][*][p]Black Bear paw bones will no longer appear separated in the X-ray view.[/p][/*][*][p]Mountain Goat horns are now properly attached to the skull in the X-ray view.[/p][/*][*][p]Wood Duck neck bones will now have names when viewed in the Harvest screen.[/p][/*][*][p]The Water Buffalo's rear leg will no longer appear detached from the pelvis in the X-ray view.[/p][/*][*][p]We’ve fixed a visual issue with the fleeing Manitoban Elk.[/p][/*][*][p]Northern Pintail wing bones will no longer clip through feathers on the harvest screen.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Audio[/b][/p][list][*][p]Dismantling deployables in multiplayer will now play the correct sound.[/p][/*][*][p]Snow Geese will now honk while flying high.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Equipment[/b][/p][list][*][p]The Fors Elite .300 rifle will no longer exhibit animation bugs when rechambering while crouching.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a clipping issue when rechambering and reloading a Zagan Varminter .22-250.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a clipping issue when chambering the Fors Elite 300 with a scope equipped.[/p][/*][*][p]The Ranger .243 is now accurate at all distances when using iron sights or TruVision.[/p][/*][*][p]Crouching before preparing a shot will no longer prevent hip-fire shots with some lever-action and pump-action weapons.[/p][/*][*][p]The 7MM Regent Magnum's point of aim is now correctly aligned at medium range when used without a scope.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where lever-action rifle animations could desynchronize during reloads while aiming.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Missions[/b][/p][list][*][p]The "Low Land" mission will no longer be blocked if player has visited the landmarks beforehand.[/p][/*][*][p]We’ve fixed an issue where the "Albertan Apex" side mission could be completed without meeting all mission requirements.[/p][/*][*][p]Taking a picture of the carcass during the "Aftermath" mission is now easier to register.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Multiplayer[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed an issue that could cause the game to temporarily freeze if the network connection was interrupted while trying to join a multiplayer game on Xbox.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Stability[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where non-high flying waterfowl would briefly freeze for players when the session host moved a significant distance away.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Trophies[/b][/p][list][*][p]The Mule Deer's final pose will no longer clip through walls in trophy lodges.[/p][/*][*][p]The fur variation for the Melanistic Pronghorn is now correctly displayed on trophies.[/p][/*][*][p]The Female Manitoban Elk head trophy will no longer have stretched textures clipping below the plaque.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug with Wood Duck Female trophies.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]UI[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where voice-overs and subtitles were mismatched.[/p][/*][*][p]The Tundra Bean Goose now has an image on the HUD when spotted.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]World[/b][/p][list][*][p]Snow deformation will no longer cover blood tracks.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Dev Diary: Making of the Pump, Flip & Fire Pack
notes.notes: [p]Check out our latest dev diary video, Behind the Boom: Making of the Pump, Flip and Fire Pack.[/p][p][/p][p]When you think about how we make theHunter: Call of the Wild, you might imagine us behind a computer screen. But believe it or not, touching real grass and metal is a pretty important part of creating the authentic hunting experience.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="n7rYvHsjXlQ;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p][b]The Pump, Flip and Fire Pack[/b] is an upcoming DLC that includes three new tactile weapons. Diversify your setup with guns that are a blast to handle, including a lever-action rifle, pump-action rifle, and singe-shot folding shotgun. [b]Available August 26th.[/b][/p]

notes.title: The Pump, Flip and Fire Pack releases August 26th
notes.notes:
[p]Howdy, Hunters! Looking to diversify your setup with guns that are a blast to handle? [/p][p][/p][p]Get your hands on the [b]Pump, Flip and Fire Pack[/b], an upcoming DLC that includes three new tactile weapons.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="XZsRiKt3n3U;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h3][b]Anantha Action .22 Mag[/b][/h3][p]A lightweight but sturdy lever-action rifle. You’ll get smooth action with low recoil, speed, and accuracy, covering small (class 1-2) animals.
[/p][p]This one comes with [b]new hollow point and jacketed hollow point .22 Magnum ammo[/b].[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-qw.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXe_sUrPd91EbrWju-4lNyVi8KPmqs_UCiBlkLIhK6nJNMahdAc78yJH6Cq3OZuVW3xDnoqFhVep8Wc-wuLF-D-BxPSdxZGQ0UBMKjQ7NzUUR-bOACfqIkW-3FRtGw1sOlLbWhgbiQ?key=QI2mI0dcv69JgNalBe2i-w"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Frost .257[/b][/h3][p]A classic magazine-fed pump-action rifle. Versatile and powerful, you can take down a wide spectrum (class 2-6) of animals.

It also comes with [b]new soft point and polymer tip .257 Roberts ammo[/b].[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-qw.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfXcrSdVsqgTTMTVc2RBKalmcLc0rYcZplSf_W5-jsbgoWNTZ27fuHdUR_5YFZZtG2-pySZeyaQH1dXsoqb1VAerSibour0zRm_nQmGIsdEA4r6HdDSU0h403MYcH8EXmuBHNl1?key=QI2mI0dcv69JgNalBe2i-w"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Giddings SSC .410 Coyote[/b][/h3][p]An ultra lightweight single-shot folding shotgun. With its break-open barrel, you can fold the gun in two and easily fit it in your backpack! It’s perfect for close range quick shots, covering a range of small to medium (class 1-5) animals. 
[/p][p]You can use it with .410 birdshot ammo and now [b]all new .410 buckshot and slug ammo[/b] too.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-qw.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXck_UxRfjwZh2EMxAkVSK-f56E4O39Ry2CDw0-MPnDPZ51QiiYZusbkfHeqcf6bP9_jZyrqr5MnbrdQhqSScwYP6ZFzD_03ABQYOP3dyloFbV1kys8zI8h3gi0DdsEsikFITMaqeg?key=QI2mI0dcv69JgNalBe2i-w"][/img][/p][p]The new pack arrives to [i]theHunter: Call of the Wild[/i] on [b]August 26th[/b] for [b]$4.99[/b]. We look forward to showing you the magic behind these weapons over the next week so keep an eye on our social media channels to see more![/p][p][/p][p]As always, this DLC will come with a game update containing some extra improvements and fixes for everyone. You can get a first look at the patch notes the day before release on August 25th.[/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary: Indigenous Roots of Askiy Ridge
notes.notes:
[p]Hey hunters![/p][p]Our names are Annette and Warren Hobart and today we hope to teach you a thing or two about how our Indigenous culture inspired the narrative and setting of the newest map, Alberta Hunting Preserve.[/p][p][/p][h2]Our Background[/h2][p]We are a proud Métis woman from Alberta and a Status First Nation man. Together, we bring generations of lived experience as Registered Trappers, land users, and cultural knowledge holders. As consultants for theHunter: Call of the Wild, we’ve worked closely with the team to ensure the game authentically represents Indigenous cultures—specifically the Métis and Cree Peoples of Alberta.
[/p][p]Throughout our careers, we've worked tirelessly to educate individuals, groups, institutions, and even other Nations about the deep Indigenous connection to the land.[/p][p][/p][p]For us this work is about ensuring Indigenous choices are heard, respected, and included in the spaces where decisions and narratives about us are being shaped. It’s about shifting power, centering Indigenous knowledge, and creating environments where our communities are not just consulted, but are leading the way.[/p][p][/p][h3]Métis, Cree, and First Nation Culture[/h3][p]In Canada, the term [b]Cree[/b] refers to one of the largest and most widespread Indigenous Nations in the country. Cree people have a distinct language (called [i]Nehiyawewin[/i]), culture, and traditional territories that span from Alberta to Quebec. The Cree Nation is made up of many different communities, each with their own governance structures and local practices, but all rooted in a shared worldview that emphasizes respect for the land, spirituality, family, and community.[/p][p][/p][p]When someone is described as a [b]Status First Nation,[/b] it means they are legally recognized under the Indian Act, a federal law in Canada that governs many aspects of Indigenous life. This status is recorded in a government registry, and it affirms the person’s identity as a member of a federally recognized First Nation. It also means they have specific rights and responsibilities tied to their Nation and to the treaties signed between First Nations and the Crown (the government of Canada).[/p][p][/p][p]While “Status” recognition offers certain legal protections, it does not define the strength or legitimacy of someone’s identity or connection to their culture. Many Indigenous people—both Status and non-Status—live deeply rooted lives in their traditions, languages, and lands.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Métis culture[/b] is a rich and distinct blend of First Nations and European ancestry, with our own language, governance, and worldview. We have a deep connection to the land, strong family networks, and a long-standing history of resilience, trade, and cultural expression—through music, storytelling, beadwork, and traditional land use.[/p][p][/p][p]Alberta is unique in Canada as the only province with legislated Métis Settlements—communities with a recognized land base and local governance. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/4f824be873c20791028621d4381b371973758c6c.png"][/img][/p][p]That uniqueness brought about some meaningful and, at times, complex conversations with theHunter team. We explored what it would look like to create a hypothetical land base in the game—one that is Indigenous-managed and culturally grounded. This idea opened the door to discussions around the realities Métis and First Nations people in Alberta face, particularly the challenges and opportunities of working together across different Nations, histories, and priorities. The result is a storyline that feels realistic. It reflects the strength, pride, and sometimes the tension that can come with inter-Nation collaboration.[/p][p][/p][h3]Hunting in Alberta[/h3][p]For us, hunting and trapping aren’t hobbies or recreational activities—they are part of a deeply rooted way of life, passed down through generations of Indigenous knowledge, experience, and respect for the land. As Registered Trappers in Eastern Alberta, we live closely with the land and pay attention to everything it tells us—watching the signs, listening to the animals, and understanding the shifts in the environment.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/d535203ee3b5e8e2d2b9778895f4e8c53968db6d.png"][/img][/p][p]Each season begins with prayer and ceremony. Before we set a trap or take a harvest, we offer thanks to the Creator and the spirits of the land. We acknowledge the animals we may take and show respect for the lives they give. These ceremonies help ground us in humility, gratitude, and spiritual responsibility. We don’t take lightly the fact that we are entering into a relationship with the land and its creatures.[/p][p][/p][p]We watch for trends on the land—the health of the animals, the balance of ecosystems, and signs of disease or overpopulation. If we see a species thriving beyond its natural balance or struggling with illness, we adjust where and what we trap to help support overall environmental health. Trapping is not just about harvesting—it’s about monitoring and maintaining the land in a way that supports all life.[/p][p][/p][p]We also harvest traditional medicines, plants, and roots—like rat root, wild mint, sweetgrass, and willow bark—which help us care for our own health and continue the practices our ancestors relied on. These are part of our seasonal routines, and they carry deep cultural significance.[/p][p][/p][p]One of our oldest guiding tools is the lunar calendar, or [i]moon cycles[/i]. Each moon—like the "Falling Leaves Moon" or the "Hard Frost Moon"—carries teachings about when to trap, when to gather, and when to rest. The moon teaches us rhythm and timing, and it helps us live in harmony with the natural world. We trap with the moon, not the clock.[/p][p][/p][h2]Translating our Indigenous Heritage into the Game[/h2][p]As Indigenous consultants for Askiy Ridge, our role has been deeply immersive and integral to the development of the preserve. From the very beginning, Warren and I were brought in not just as advisors, but as cultural stewards—ensuring every detail reflects the true spirit, traditions, and knowledge systems of the Indigenous peoples of Alberta, specifically the Métis and Cree communities.[/p][p][/p][p]From the portrayal of the wildlife and landscapes of Alberta, to music, traditional hunting methods, the main hunting lodge and cabins, characters, and storylines, we’ve infused the game with real traditions, perspectives, and practices passed down through generations. We’ve helped shape the characters, their voices, and even the naming conventions of the game’s regions—making sure they are grounded in place, history, and meaning.[/p][p][/p][h3]The Main Lodge[/h3][p]Our input has helped shape both the interior and exterior design of the main hunting lodge and cabins—ensuring they reflect the practical and cultural elements of Indigenous life in Alberta. We spent a lot of time working with the team to ensure that every detail reflected the lived experience of Indigenous land users—particularly Métis and Cree families with deep roots in the fur trade era.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/24d4975e0c26ecfc11d5237fdd45a656f829d815.png"][/img][/p][p]One important feature we shared was the traditional tongue and groove method used in cabin building. This is a wood joinery technique where one board has a groove cut into it and another has a corresponding “tongue” that fits snugly inside. It creates a strong, weather-resistant seal without the need for nails or screws, which was essential for building warm and sturdy cabins in remote areas using limited tools. This method is still used today in many traditional trapper cabins across Alberta.[/p][p][/p][p]We also guided the team in adding meaningful interior touches—like handmade furniture, woven rugs, trade blankets, and leatherwork—items commonly found in Indigenous homes. These were not just decorative, but functional and often created by hand using local materials. The presence of beadwork, antler-handled tools, and traditional artwork helped give each cabin a sense of story and identity.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/863368dd303988dcfc85d1e957b95ea473846052.png"][/img][/p][p]These cabins represent more than shelter; they reflect self-sufficiency, resilience, and pride in our way of life. The team didn’t just design a space—they captured the spirit of home for many Indigenous people who’ve lived and worked on the land for generations.[/p][p][/p][h3]Character Design[/h3][p]We also worked with the design team to ensure the characters are authentic in their appearance, including their clothing, gear, and mannerisms. Warren and I were deeply involved in shaping the characters to ensure they reflect real Indigenous people—not stereotypes or generic representations. From their clothing and physical appearance to their personalities, backstories, and ways of speaking, we worked closely with the team to build characters that are rooted in authentic Métis and Cree worldviews.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-qw.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdBny4n1qBa2-fGFyvADiw3F9z82at0IciNVnWBjJ5qdJ05Cn4p02KyocUUga8P31Qy1diVA0XaRwFvsSYXRq35s66SApJRWVn3hdlG-gVhqrlDN3WuEckvORjvJhg-3ZJ6voAf?key=yTNnCCc2Rw_0GjKdvFXDVw"][/img][i]Janine Armstrong, main character of Askiy Ridge’s story.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]We discussed traditional and practical clothing styles—things like moccasins, sashes, fur-lined jackets, and other pieces influenced by both the fur trade and land-based living. These aren’t just costumes—they reflect identity, utility, and cultural pride. We also paid close attention to the characters’ tools, gear, and accessories, ensuring they reflect the resourcefulness and craftsmanship of Indigenous trappers and hunters.[/p][p][/p][p]But beyond appearance, we helped shape the character arcs and personalities. We emphasized the importance of humility, respect for the land, kinship ties, and traditional knowledge. For example, we guided the team on how an Elder character might speak or carry themselves—with patience, wisdom, and humor—and how a younger character might be in a learning role, full of questions, trying to reconnect with the land or their culture.[/p][p][/p][p]We also made sure that characters weren’t just placed in the story—but that their roles had cultural depth and meaning. Each character represents something larger than themselves—whether it’s the role of knowledge keeper, hunter, helper, or protector of tradition. Even their emotional expressions and dialogue were shaped to align with the way Indigenous people speak—grounded, relational, and often layered with teaching.[/p][p][/p][p]Our goal was simple: to make the characters feel real to Indigenous players and respectfully educational to non-Indigenous audiences.[/p][p][/p][h3]The Sasquatch[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/cc0769ca91b83da5611764cd8d357f59ef9fa392.png"][/img][i]A sign of our beloved cryptid?[/i][/p][p][/p][p]One of the more exciting contributions was influencing theHunter team to include a Sasquatch figure into the storyline—honoring Indigenous oral histories and legends that are still very much alive across the land today. This addition is incredibly meaningful to us—not just because of the legend itself, but because it acknowledges the spiritual and mysterious relationship Indigenous people have with the land. It also adds depth and mystery to the game, rooted in real beliefs held by many Indigenous communities.[/p][p]For many Indigenous cultures across North America, Sasquatch—known by different names such as [i]Sabe[/i], [i]Bukwas[/i], or [i]Môhkomân[/i]—is more than just a legend or a creature of curiosity. Sasquatch holds deep spiritual and cultural significance as a being that exists in the space between the natural and supernatural worlds.[/p][p][/p][p]In many Cree and other Indigenous teachings, Sasquatch is understood as a keeper of the land—a watcher, protector, or messenger who reminds us of our responsibilities to live in balance with nature. Some teachings describe him as a shape-shifter or spiritual being who reveals himself only to those who carry respect, humility, and a strong connection to the land. These stories are passed down through oral tradition—not as myths, but as teachings about how to live responsibly and with reverence for all living things.[/p][p][/p][p]Sasquatch is not just a part of our culture—it’s part of our lived experience. We’ve spent many nights deep in the bush, away from the noise of the world, listening closely to the sounds of the forest. We’ve heard wood knocks echo through the trees, unexplained vocalizations, and even found strange structures and footprints. Those moments aren’t scary to us—they’re spiritual. They remind us that we’re never truly alone out there and that the land is alive with memory, spirit, and presence.[/p][p][/p][p]Including Sasquatch in this game wasn’t just about adding mystery—it was about honoring the unseen knowledge that Indigenous people have carried for generations.[/p][p][/p][h2]Working with theHunter: Call of the Wild team[/h2][p]For both of us, being part of this project has been incredibly meaningful. It’s not every day that Indigenous people are invited to help shape something from the ground up—especially in the world of gaming. The development team has shown us a level of respect and collaboration that we deeply appreciate. Together, we’ve created something that not only entertains but also reflects the beauty, strength, and complexity of our cultures. We hope that players walk away with more than just a great gaming experience—we hope they leave with a deeper understanding of the land, the stories, and the people who’ve called it home for generations.[/p][p][/p][p]We believe in the inclusion of Indigenous voices at the table—not as an afterthought, but from the start. The development team has honored that commitment, and we’re proud to say this project represents one of the most respectful and accurate portrayals of Indigenous life in a gaming platform to date. It’s rare to see Métis culture represented in video games, let alone in a way that respects the richness of our history, our connection to the land, and our way of life. Watching it come to life in the game was powerful—it’s a preserve that blends mystery, respect, and culture all in one.[/p]

notes.title: Alberta Hunting Preserve is Out Now!
notes.notes: [p]Are you bold enough to brave the snow? Head on over to [b]Alberta Hunting Preserve[/b], otherwise known as Askiy Ridge![/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://youtu.be/qoI4toJKqZ0"][/dynamiclink][/p][h3]Buy Alberta now![/h3][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3570290/theHunter_Call_of_the_Wild__Alberta_Hunting_Preserve/"][/dynamiclink][/p][h2]Alberta Hunting Preserve[/h2][p]Alberta introduces 13 missions that immerse you in the Canadian winter through the lifestyle of First Nation Albertans. Help the warden and local experts maintain the preserve on the trail of the secretive Sasquatch.[/p][p]Explore pine-covered peaks down to frost-swept grasslands through deep snow, but watch out for falling trees, a sign of Askiy Ridge’s star animal! The [b]North American Beaver[/b] is a brand new species with unique behavior to match their hardworking personality. Just as they once destroyed your tents, they will destroy the trees around you for the good of their dam. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/157debd283a7af886c980e51acb7f28b7edf0fab.jpg"][/img][/p][p]With a total of [b]19 species[/b], this preserve introduces[b] 8 new animals[/b], including the [b]Manitoban Elk[/b], [b]Wood Bison[/b], [b]Dusky Grouse[/b], [b]Northern Pintail[/b], [b]Wood Duck[/b], [b]Snow Goose[/b], and [b]Woodland Caribou[/b]. [/p][p]Some familiar faces include the [b]Moose[/b], [b]Black Bear[/b], [b]Gray Wolf[/b], [b]Bighorn Sheep[/b], [b]Mule Deer[/b], [b]Whitetail Deer[/b], [b]Mountain Goat[/b], [b]Pronghorn[/b], [b]Canada Goose[/b], [b]Mallard[/b], and [b]Ring-Necked Pheasant[/b].[/p][p]The preserve also comes with a new gun, the[b] Laperriere Outrider .30-30[/b]. You can get it either as a reward for completing the story, or at the in-game shop for in-game currency. The new .30-.30 is  a lever-action rifle with a side-loading and side-ejecting design suited for small to medium game and compatible with a wide range of rifle scopes.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/94c24dec0d44a89166873c4acc39ab502fc333c3.png"][/img][/p][h2]The Snowfall Update[/h2][p]Releasing with Alberta Hunting Preserve is Snowfall Update, available for everyone! You can read the patch notes for the Snowfall Update here.[/p][p]BUFFALO PLAID UTILITY OUTFIT[/p][p]Regardless of whether or not you own the new preserve, you can access a new Canada-themed full outfit set! The Buffalo Plaid Utility outfit is now purchasable with in-game currency for everyone through the in-game store.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/d5195af7481f96a1367d9c8ca05b08cbe2336ea9.jpg"][/img][/p][p]NEW GREAT ONE: THE MULE DEER[/p][p]If you’re lucky, you may come across a Mule Deer Great One. The new great one has unique fur types and racks. We can’t wait to see what combinations you find![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/cd2bd10344e5ad6228e13965d21c873a4621cd93.png"][/img][/p][p]7 REMASTERS[/p][p]We have given some extra love to existing animals in this update.[/p][p][b]The Bighorn Sheep[/b]: New models. Redone fur variations. New fur variations added. All TruRACs have been replaced with new, more realistic models. New audio calls.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/eacf736e8a0a33e44bde21532f65765e56714159.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]The Pronghorn[/b]: New models. Redone fur variations. New fur variations added. All TruRACs have been replaced with new, more realistic models. Additional animations.[/p][p][b]Mountain Goat[/b]: New models. Redone fur variations. Some redone animations. New audio calls.[/p][p][b]Canada Goose[/b]: New models. Redone plumage variations. New plumage variations. Some animation improvements.[/p][p][b]Gray Wolf[/b]: New models. Redone fur variations. New fur variations. New calls. Fixes and improvements to wolf animation and behavior.[/p][p][b]Grant Caribou (renamed)[/b]: New models. Redone fur variations. Animation improvements.[/p][p][b]Mule Deer[/b]: New model. Redone fur variations. New fur variations added.[/p][p]OTHER HIGHLIGHTS[/p][list][*][p]The Mule Deer population was reset on Parque Fernando, Rancho del Arroyo, and Silver Ridge Peaks[/p][/*][*][p]In snowy climates, snow will now appear on animal coats[/p][/*][*][p]Two new multimounts have been added for the North American Beaver and Mule Deer[/p][/*][*][p]The world map has been redesigned to allow for more locations in the future[/p][/*][*][p]The tutorials have been improved[/p][/*][*][p]The .30-.30 ammo has been retuned to improve muzzle velocity and reduce wind resistance[/p][/*][/list][p]There are lots of other things to look forward to in the update, so check out [url="https://callofthewild.thehunter.com/snowfall-update-patch-notes-june-16th-2025/"]the full patch notes [/url]here! [/p]

The UI will not display the current setting until the player presses the "Use Skill" button again.[/p][/*][*][p]Saltwater Crocodiles may be difficult to “Spot” from certain angles.[/p][/*][*][p]Feral Goats can run in circles while trying to flee in some places in Emerald Coast Australia.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Equipment[/b][/p][list][*][p]Players must load their weapons before entering the shooting range, even though they have unlimited ammo once in the range.[/p][/*][*][p]All backpacks, regardless of size or color, have the same in-game model when seen on the player.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Dog[/b][/p][list][*][p]The audio for the barks does not seem to be balanced properly based on the dog’s relative position.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Missions[/b][/p][list][*][p]The “Albertan Apex” mission in Askiy Ridge Hunting Preserve can be completed faster than intended.[/p][/*][*][p]Light Brown pumas shot prior to the Outback Update are invisible when placed in the trophy room on Parque Fernando.[/p][list][*][p]Developer’s note: This has been a very challenging bug to fix. As of the Outback Update, anyone progressing this mission for the first time should see their trophies without issue. Unfortunately, players who have already placed a Light Brown Puma on the stand will still see an invisible trophy for now.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][b]World[/b][/p][list][*][p]Players may fall out of the world in a certain spot on the ice south of Zverolova Hill on Medved.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Graphics[/b][/p][list][*][p]Players may notice a transparent, repeating ascending column while placing Ground Blinds.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Audio[/b][/p][list][*][p]Hog Deer sounds like Roe Deer.[/p][/*][/list][p]If you're experiencing any issues with the game that aren't mentioned in this list, please reach out to our[url="https://support.thehunter.com/"] Support Team[/url].[/p]

notes.title: Alberta Hunting Preserve｜Coming Soon
notes.notes:
Hey there Hunters,

Last November, during the Winter Preview Showcase, you might remember that we teased a new map, set to arrive in Summer 2025. Well Summer 2025 is almost here!

We’re excited to reveal your next hunting destination is in [b]Canada[/b]. [b]Alberta Hunting Preserve[/b], otherwise known as [b]Askiy Ridge[/b], is coming soon.

[previewyoutube=hEEN_uvepFg;full][/previewyoutube]

Here you can discover, track, and hunt 19 local species both old and new, including the [b]North American Beaver[/b], the [b]Manitoban Elk[/b], [b]Snow Geese[/b], [b]Dusky Grouse[/b], [b]Whitetail Deer[/b], [b]Gray Wolf[/b], and [b]Wood Bison[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/25a4ff413d0ac7598aaf73edb5ca17e90c1f8f13.jpg[/img]

On Askiy Ridge, a new adventure awaits with 13 missions and the opportunity to explore everything from the pine-covered peaks down to the frost-swept grasslands in search of the perfect hunting spot.

Just be careful of falling trees, a sure sign of the preserve’s most hardworking creature.

Along with the new preserve, you will also get the Laperriere Outrider .30-30, a new lever-action rifle. This rifle has a side-loading and side-ejecting design and is suited for small to medium game.

You can wishlist Alberta Hunting Preserve now!

Keep an eye on our social channels for more reveals.

notes.title: Rapid Hunt Rifle Pack – Out Now!
notes.notes:
[h2]Add three new semi-autos to your hunting collection[/h2]
The Rapid Hunt Rifle Pack is out now and includes three tough-built and reliable semi-automatic rifles aptly named for their rapid firing power.

[previewyoutube=EoCemJZZmVQ;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]PERRY .308[/h3]
With powerful recoil management and gas-operated long-stroke piston action, every shot will feel just as effective as the last. 

The PERRY has .308 ammunition and is built for medium to big game hunting, covering classes 4-8.

[h3]HANSSON .30-06[/h3]
Designed for quick action and hip fire and built with great attention to detail, you’ll get extremely smooth action, allowing you to land fast follow-up shots. 

The HANSSON has .30-06 ammunition and is another great fit for medium to big game, also covering classes 4-8.

[h3]QUIST REAPER 7.62X39[/h3]
With the force of 7.62x39mm rounds and the precision hunters crave, this is a timeless choice. It’s easy to use and rocks a brand new ammo type. 

The QUIST REAPER is great for small to medium game, covering classes 2-6.

You can find the Rapid Hunt Rifle Pack across all platforms for $4.99

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3447720/theHunter_Call_of_the_Wild__Rapid_Hunt_Rifle_Pack/

[h2]March Update[/h2]
In addition to the new Rifle Pack, today you’ll also get a new patch with bug fixes. Check out the full [url=https://callofthewild.thehunter.com/patch-notes-march25/]Patch Notes [/url]for more details.

[h2]Highlights[/h2]
Looking for Tahr? You’ll start to see them out on [url=https://callofthewild.thehunter.com/home/dlc/reserves/thehunter-call-of-the-wild-te-awaroa-national-park/]Te Awaroa[/url]! With that, the Chamois will also get a population reset.

[h2]Community Challenges[/h2]
You might notice something new on your menu screen. The first Community Challenge starts in 2 days and offers exclusive cosmetics for everyone who participates. 

We’ll have to work together to unlock the rewards, so prepare by making sure you’re geared up for medium-sized game.

[h2]Livestream[/h2]
Don’t forget that we’re hosting a launch stream with Vivi and Tommy at 16:30 CET, 8:30AM PST on [url=https://www.twitch.tv/expansiveworlds]Twitch[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/@ExpansiveWorlds]YouTube[/url]. We’ll be focusing on the new weapon pack from the perspective of a lead animator. We hope to see you there!

notes.title: Decide which animal gets extra fur types next year!
notes.notes:
[h2]Vote, vote, vote![/h2]
We're hosting a poll right now where you can choose which animal, from a short list, gets extra fur variations next year. This poll is ONLY being done on our official Discord, so you'll need to join to participate. When you're there, head over to # cotw-polls to vote and choose the @ Polls role to get notified for future polls.

[url=https://avlche.com/THDiscord]You have 72 hours to vote![/url]

[h2]FAQ[/h2]
[b]How many variations will you be adding?[/b]
It will be decided during production. However, we have a goal of maintaining a consistent distribution of rarity so depending on the chosen animal, the number might vary.

[b]How many species will get extra fur variations?[/b]
At the moment, we plan to add extra fur variations only for the top-voted animal.

[b]When can I see the new variations being added to the game?[/b]
If you followed our Community Weapon Pack updates, you probably already know that adding new content to the game takes time. We currently aim at the second half of 2025 for the new variations to arrive.

[b]Do you plan to organize more polls like this in the future?[/b]
Yes. We often post these kinds of polls on our Official Discord. In fact, you should keep an eye on our official channels again next week!

notes.title: The Winter Hotfix is now live!
notes.notes:
Greetings Hunters!

A new hotfix has been released to resolve some of the bugs that have arisen since the launch of the Winter Update. Let's take a look at the details!

[h2]Developer’s Notes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Some players have been having problems with their game progress not being saved. If your game is on a PC, sometimes, Windows Security might stop you from reaching the Documents folder (that's where your save files are). So you need to allow (or whitelist) your apps to access it. Plus, using Norton Anti-Virus may wrongly block parts of your save data thinking they are harmful. So, try to check your computer's security settings to make sure they are not stopping the game from saving your progress. For more help, visit our support page.
[*] It's been pointed out by a few players that a picture of Florian Jansen, who is the key contact for Salzwiesen Park, can't be found in the Codex. This is done on purpose. Florian values his privacy, and didn’t want his picture publicly available.
[/list]
[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]

[h3]EQUIPMENT[/h3]
[list]
[*] Decoys and callers associated with birds found in Salzwiesen Park which can also be found in other locations should now be available if the player only purchases Salzwiesen Park.
[/list]
[h3]ANIMALS[/h3]
[list]
[*] Upland birds such as Pheasants and Grouses should be more reactive to the threatening presence of players and dogs. They should also be better at trying to fly away when there’s no nearby available cover.
[*] Waterfowl should be less wary again, and land more frequently.
[/list]
[h3]DOG[/h3]
[list]
[*] The “Flush” command should now always display on the dog wheel when it is available for use.
[*] Birds should be less wary of being pointed at by the dog.
[/list]
[h3]TROPHIES[/h3]
[list]
[*] When replacing existing trophies in a Trophy Lodge, the swapped trophies should appear normally again.
[/list]
[h3]SYSTEM[/h3]
[list]
[*] The game should no longer momentarily freeze or stutter when you shoot at a target on the shooting range with a shotgun loaded with birdshot.
[/list]
[h3]MULTIPLAYER[/h3]
[list]
[*] Ground birds should react appropriately when flushed by a host.
[*] Waterfowl should appear normally in Multiplayer games again.
[*] The Clay Thrower should now be working well in Multiplayer.
[/list]
[h3]UI[/h3]
[list]
[*] The placement of the new Hunting Pressure Tooltip should now be away from other information boxes to prevent overlap.
[*] PlayStation and Xbox users should now see the correct description for the German Shorthaired Pointer.
[*] We've fixed an issue where the error message displayed after aborting the purchase of a dog package from the Expert Hunting Dog menu couldn’t be closed without closing the entire menu.
[/list]

Also check out the updated [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/518790/discussions/5/3825284962834792949/]known issues[/url] list.

notes.title: Winter Update, Salzwiesen Park, Pointer, & Bolt-Action Rifles
notes.notes:
Howdy hunters,

Today you can enjoy a compact hunting experience in [b]Salzwiesen Park[/b], find and flush waterfowl with the [b]German Shorthaired Pointer[/b], and take your shooting skills to new levels with the [b]Hunters’ Choice: Bolt-Action Rifle Pack[/b] – all available now.

Save 11% on all three DLCs with the [b]Winter Hunting Bundle[/b] -

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/47553/theHunter_Call_of_the_Wild__Winter_Hunting_Bundle/

Also available today is the Winter Update, introducing all-new [i]Hunter Challenges[/i], two new [i]Great Ones[/i], and much more! 

[h2]Salzwiesen Park[/h2]
Explore the salt marsh habitat and hunt a wide range of waterfowl and small game. Plus, sharpen your shooting skills solo or compete against friends at the Clay Shooting Range–our new gameplay feature–unique to Salzwiesen Park. 

[previewyoutube=vZ3KA9PqGiw;full][/previewyoutube]
Salzwiesen Park is home to 15 different animal species, including 2 brand-new waterfowl.
[list]
[*] Greylag Goose
[*] Tundra Bean Goose
[*] Ring-Necked Pheasant
[*] Black Grouse
[*] European Rabbit
[*] Common Raccoon
[*] Raccoon Dog
[*] Red Fox
[*] Goldeneye
[*] Eurasian Teal
[*] Mallard
[*] Eurasian Wigeon
[*] Tufted Duck
[*] Gadwall [b]← New [/b]
[*] Ferruginous Duck [b]← New[/b]
[/list]
We also have not forgotten about a new caller for the Gadwall and new decoys for the Gadwall and Ferruginous duck. This DLC also includes the versatile new GOPI 10 GRAND shotgun that shares all 3 types of ammo with the Strandberg 10SA.
[list]
[*] 10 GA Plastic Birdshot Class 1-2 
[*] 10 GA Plastic Buckshot Class 4-7
[*] 10 GA Plastic Slug Class 6-9
[/list]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3244810/theHunter_Call_of_the_Wild__Salzwiesen_Park/

[h2]German Shorthaired Pointer[/h2]
Meet your newest hunting companion! Designed to point you in the right direction of your desired prey, it will–on your command–leap and bound its way towards all but the largest of predators, making them much easier to target. 

Owners of multiple dog breeds can also use the new [i]Expert Dog[/i] feature, which comes with this [i]Winter Update[/i]. This new feature will allow you to customize your expert hunting dog by enhancing one dog with the skills of two. For example, by combining the skills of a Pointer and a Retriever, you can train your dog to skillfully flush out birds and efficiently retrieve them after you’ve taken your shot. Pretty neat! This lovely companion comes with 6 different fur color variations.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3244800/theHunter_Call_of_the_Wild__German_Shorthaired_Pointer/

[h2]Hunters’ Choice: Bolt-Action Rifle Pack[/h2]
Brought to life by you, our incredible community, this new pack includes three bolt-action rifles suited for engaging a variety of different-sized species. 
[list]
[*] [b]Vallgarda .375[/b] - Uses .375 Polymer-Tip or Soft-Point rounds, for Classes 7-9, and mounts standard rifle scopes.
[*] [b]Johansson .450[/b] - Uses .450 Polymer-Tip and Soft-Point rounds, for Classes 4-7, and mounts standard rifle scopes.
[*] [b]Fors Elite .300[/b] - Uses 7.62x35mm Polymer-Tip and Soft-Point rounds, for Classes 3-6, mounts standard rifle scopes.
[/list]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3244820/theHunter_Call_of_the_Wild__Hunters_Choice_BoltAction_Rifle_Pack/

[h2]Winter Update[/h2]
[h3]New Features[/h3]
[b]5 New Multi Mounts for the Trophy Lodge.[/b]
[list]
[*] [i]Partners in Crime[/i]: Created by 2 Red Foxes.
[*] [i]Flying Pheast[/i]: Created with a Red Fox and a Ring-Necked Pheasant.
[*] [i]Landlubber Lineup[/i]: Created from a Black Grouse, Ring-necked Pheasant, Graylag Goose, and a Tundra Bean Goose.
[*] [i]The Three Ducketeers[/i]: Created with a Eurasian Wigeon, Gadwall, and a Ferruginous Duck.
[*] [i]Duck out[/i]: Requires all 7 ducks: Eurasian Teal, Eurasian Wigeon, Ferruginous Duck, Gadwall, Goldeneye, Mallard, and a Tufted Duck.
[/list]
[b]Hunt Club Beta has been upgraded to Challenges[/b]
[list]
[*] Players can now select Daily and Weekly challenges to pursue from a selection of various options.
[*] The options will include both hunting and photography challenges.
[/list]
[b]Two new Great Ones have entered the wilderness.[/b]
[list]
[*] [i]Red Fox[/i] - 9 variations.
[*] [i]Ring-necked Pheasant[/i] -  8 variations.
[/list]
[h3]Improvements[/h3]
[b]ANIMALS[/b]
[list]
[*] Red Foxes received a few improvements in this patch. Their animations were completely overhauled, and behaviors got slightly adjusted (their populations in the existing reserves have been reset).
[*] European Rabbits have been remastered (their populations in the existing reserves have been reset).
[*] Cinnamon Teals have been remastered.
[*] Flight and landing characteristics for birds have been updated for a more realistic hunting experience.
[*] Birds should more consistently land near decoys now.
[*] Waterfowl should have more realistic reactions to different situations.
[*] Upland Birds should more consistently try to hide, and birds flushing should now have a chance to flee in any direction.
[*] The Grounded Check on Upland Birds should be more accurate when the birds are close to the ground or landing, but not yet on the ground.
[*] Black Grouse, Tufted Duck, Eurasian Wigeon, Eurasian Teal, Cinnamon Teal, and Red Fox audio have been improved.
[*] We’ve added minor improvements to animations and X-ray models for multiple older species.
[*] Furs on Axis Deer, Blackbucks, Fallow Deer, and Reindeer got improved.
[/list]
[b]DOG[/b]
[list]
[*] The Dog’s Command Wheel has been completely redone with nested menus that allow for the Pointer and Expert Hunting Dog commands to be fully integrated into the UI.
[*] We’ve improved the Dog’s animations so it looks more at their owner.
[*] We’ve upgraded the Dog status UI to pulse when the Dog’s status changes if the player hasn't given a command.
[*] It is now easier to see the Dog’s outline when it’s hidden behind various obstacles.
[/list]
[b]UI[/b]
[list]
[*] When accessing the storage menu, the following changes have been made to improve navigation.
[*] Only the weapons category will be open by default.
[*] Only one category of items (e.g. weapons, sights, etc.) can be opened at a time.
[*] Opening a category will close any other open categories.
[*] A new tooltip feature has been added for hunting pressure. Now, when you hover your cursor over the hunting pressure area on the map, a tooltip will appear showing the current level of hunting pressure, and explaining the effects. 
[/list]
[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[b]GAMEPLAY[/b]
[list]
[*] We’ve fixed an issue with birdshot rounds only showing a single trajectory trace on the X-ray screen.
[*] An issue where players would make less noise if they started aiming while sprinting than they would aiming while walking got fixed.
[/list]
[b]EQUIPMENT[/b]
[list]
[*] The default reticle on the Goshawk Redeye 2-4x20 Handgun Scope has been reverted to the original one.
[*] The sight picture with the Ascent 1-4X24 Scope on the F.L. Sporter rifle has been adjusted to be more similar to other rifles with that scope.
[*] We’ve improved various shotgun animations.
[*] An issue where several scope preview images were flipped horizontally in the storage menu was addressed.
[*] We’ve fixed an issue that could cause Picatinny rails to show up on weapons when they weren’t supposed to.
[*] We’ve fixed an issue that could cause duck callers not to work under certain conditions.
[/list]
[b]ANIMALS[/b]
[list]
[*] The Need Zone markers on the map will now persist even after one of the animals linked to the Need Zone is killed, as long as there are still other known living animals associated with that same Need Zone.
[*] Aggressive animals should no longer get stuck while attacking nearby players.
[*] Waterfowl should be a bit less vocal while flying.
[*] Animals should not get stuck next to rivers as often - this was pretty common in Cuatro Colinas.
[*] The neck of the Puma no longer shrinks when performing the “smelling” animation.
[*] An issue where Grey Wolves would react oddly when shot while drinking was fixed.
[*] We’ve fixed some issues with the female Nilgai.
[*] Resolved a problem where animals could get trapped if they couldn't find a path to escape while fleeing.
[*] Some visual issues with the wings on Greylag Geese were fixed.
[*] Killing Waterfowl creates significantly less hunting pressure than before.
[*] We’ve fixed a model issue with the male Banteng.
[*] An issue where the Tiger’s face didn’t consistently show the correct wrinkle textures was fixed.
[*] Certain animals will no longer move incorrectly when standing up after being spooked.
[/list]
[b]DOG[/b]
[list]
[*] An issue where a Retriever Dog could not find harvests that were shot after it was sent to retrieve them was fixed.
[*] Petting your Dog in Trophy Lodges should look a bit better.
[*] We’ve fixed an issue where Retrieving cost more Focus than intended.
[*] Dogs will no longer spawn too far away from tower outposts in Emerald Coast Australia.
[*] We’ve fixed an issue where Dogs would not follow the player when they used a boat.
[*] Resolved several animation problems observed when a player was seen interacting with their Dog in Multiplayer.
[*] An issue where the Dog’s status bar would flicker while using binoculars was addressed.
[*] Jackrabbits should now look more accurate when being carried by the Retriever.
[*] The Dog will now be more attentive when predators are nearby, even if told to lay down.
[*] Dogs will no longer pant excessively after retrieving a harvest.
[*] Resolved a problem where the Dog command wheel would become unresponsive after switching hunting reserves if the player was located in an outpost when leaving the previous reserve.
[*] Dogs will now have fewer problems with navigating around rocks on newer reserves.
[*] The Dog will now show appropriate reverence for the Ban Gufa landmark on Sundarpatan, and wait patiently for the player outside the cave.
[*] We’ve fixed an issue with the animations for the female Bloodhound.
[/list]
[b]MISSIONS[/b]
[list]
[*] We’ve fixed an issue where there was no audio associated with cleaning up trash during the “Beauty of Nature” mission on Emerald Coast Australia.
[*] The animal in the last mission on Cuatro Colinas will no longer become unresponsive to the player.
[/list]
[b]SYSTEM[/b]
[list]
[*] The EGS version of the game will no longer get stuck on a black screen while being run from outside the EGS launcher.
[*] Resolved a problem where discovering numerous Need Zones on a map could result in a significant drop in FPS.
[/list]
[b]MULTIPLAYER[/b]
[list]
[*] We’ve fixed an issue with animation synchronization for animals in Multiplayer.
[*] Changed numerous connection error messages to be more accurate.
[*] We’ve addressed an issue that could occasionally cause the game to freeze during a host migration.
[/list]
[b]WORLD[/b]
[list]
[*] We’ve fixed some miscellaneous item placement issues in Sundarpatan Nepal and Emerald Coast Australia.
[*] Resolved a problem in the generation of navigation paths where movable objects were creating unnecessary obstacles.
[*] We’ve fixed a floating trash bin on Mississippi Acres Reserve and added some additional item placement improvements.
[*] An issue that could cause the player to be teleported to an unsafe location after running into the water from a particular dock on Revontuli Coast was fixed.
[/list]
[b]UI[/b]
[list]
[*] Players who unlink their APEX Connect accounts should be prompted to restore them again when relaunching the game in the next 24 hours.
[*] We’ve fixed an issue with eye reflections not showing up on the harvest screen.
[*] Resolved a problem where the main menu options for Multiplayer and the DLC Store wouldn't update accurately following a change in network connection status.
[*] We’ve fixed some landmark titles in the codex that were inconsistently capitalized.
[/list]
Happy hunting! 

Having issues? Check our [url=https://callofthewild.thehunter.com/known-issues-list/]known issues list[/url] and reach out to our [url=https://support.thehunter.com/]Support Team[/url].

notes.title: Steam Awards 2024
notes.notes:
Hunters,

We’re entering the holiday season and find ourselves reminiscing on the almost eight years of developing theHunter: Call of the Wild. As we celebrate how far we’ve come and the exciting things on the horizon, we hope you’ll consider supporting us in this year's Steam Labor of Love award.
Let’s take a look at the last year!

We released two new hunting locations: The new Salzwiesen Park (for birds and other small game) and Sundarpatan Nepal Hunting Reserve (for those that would rather be hunted)
Following last year’s addition of the Retriever, the kennel got a little bit bigger with a new loyal friend - the German Shorthaired Pointer. And with 3 dogs on the roster, you can now combine 2 dog traits with the Expert Dog Feature.

The weapons have gotten lots of attention with customizable crosshairs and the addition of the High Caliber Weapon Pack, Odin being a popular choice. We also asked you to collaborate with us on the development of the newly released Hunters’ Choice: Bolt Action Pack, a pack close to our heart because we created it based on popularity polls from the community and took you through some of the development process on the way to launch.
And the future?

We stand today on the cusp of some thrilling updates for the future. Next year, as revealed in the [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oNKN0B_FrF4]Winter Preview Show[/url], we'll be releasing two big reserves along with many other updates and content drops.
We’re grateful for the incredible community we’ve built and can’t wait to continue this journey with you.

// theHunter: Call of the Wild Team

notes.title: Dev Diary: Master Clay Shooting in Salzwiesen Park
notes.notes:
Hi! My name is Björn Vallgårda Öjlert and I’ve recently returned to work as a Principal Game Designer on theHunter: Call of the Wild. I have a long history of working with the franchise starting as a Game Designer on theHunter: Classic all the way back in 2010. I was also part of the team responsible for the initial release of theHunter: Call of the Wild in 2017.

As a game designer, my work primarily involves defining and tweaking the gameplay. For example, how weapons, ballistics, and damage work or how animals go about their daily need zone schedule. For the Salzwiesen Park my main contributions revolved around the clay shooting range and some improvements to the bird hunting gameplay.

[h2]A Bird Hunters Paradise[/h2]

Salzwiesen Park is a more specialized experience compared to our previous maps with the main theme revolving around hunting birds and small game using shotguns. It’s smaller in size compared to the regular reserves and can be viewed as a sort of experiment where we’ve tried to really get into a specific type of hunting and make that as enjoyable as possible.

Of course, we could not make this happen without filling the park with a vast array of bird species including two brand new ducks - Gadwall Duck and Ferruginous Duck, and adding a powerful 10 GA U/O shotgun.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/85f62d7192443b3b6206ee9fb92a284e2d570d26.png[/img]

[h2]The Clay Shooting Range[/h2]

Designing the clay shooting range for Salzwiesen Park was an interesting experience as I also designed the original clay shooting range for theHunter: Classic. Even though I had a basic understanding of clay shooting from field trips to a local range back in the Classic days, considerable time has passed since then. As a result, I had to begin this process with extensive research.

That’s when I came across clay shooting ranges that combine multiple modes such as Skeet & Trap and this became the basis for my new CotW design. Essentially, my aim was to create something that clearly improves upon theHunter Classic’s format. What better approach to accomplish this than by introducing a range with new types of clay shooting never seen before in theHunter?

The Salzwiesen Park clay shooting range can be found near the main lodge, which is also where you start your adventure on this map. Similar to previous CotW ranges, it is very much a sandbox type of experience that gives players a lot of freedom to use it any way they want. It’s a combination of a Skeet and Trap range, with all the platforms and trap machines that go along with that.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27000850/73bf0a29b8e3a5d9eb67979aa744b6994430e4be.png[/img]

Skeet platforms are orange and Trap platforms are blue. To use the range, simply walk up to any of these platforms and press the button indicated on the screen to launch a target. Hits and misses are scored and can be viewed directly on the screen while on a platform. 

At the back of each trap lane, there is a score reset button and you can also access a weapon cache there if you want to try out different weapons. This is also where you find one of the most interesting features of the range; a control tower that allows you to switch between several trap configurations.

Here you’ll find all the typical Trap and Skeet modes, including Single Trap, Double Trap, Single Skeet, and Double Skeet. But I also threw in some unconventional random modes to spice things up, including a “sporting” mode where targets can be launched from any machine on the range for maximum confusion and chaos.

The range can be enjoyed alone or with friends. There are no set rules so you’ll have to agree on that among yourselves. Follow real-life rules if you know them, or make up your own. I hope you’ll have as much fun on this range as we did when making it!

[h2]Bird Hunting Improvements[/h2]

We've made several adjustments and improvements to the bird hunting experience based on community feedback. The most notable changes will be observed in the movements and behaviors of birds while taking off and landing. Beyond these visible changes, we've also subtly tweaked the birds' senses.

Sparked your interest? Great because, the latter is one of the things that I worked on, so let me elaborate. Essentially, all duck species now lack a sense of smell, but we've slightly heightened their other senses to balance this. This alteration mirrors real life, where ducks have a very poor sense of smell. Furthermore, in response to direct community feedback, I've reduced the distance at which ducks 'auto-spook' when flying near players. This change should make bird hunting less frustrating, particularly in situations where birds fly in close proximity to your hiding spot.

That’s it for me! I hope you will enjoy what Salzwiesen Park has to offer.

Happy hunting and clay shooting!

notes.title: Winter Preview Show - New Hunting Content Coming this December!
notes.notes:
Howdy, Hunters!

Thank you for tuning in to our first ever Winter Preview Showcase! We had so much fun doing the show, and can’t wait for you to experience all the new content when it arrives on all platforms on December 3.

[previewyoutube=oNKN0B_FrF4;full][/previewyoutube]

Wishlist now!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3244810/theHunter_Call_of_the_Wild__Salzwiesen_Park/

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3244820/theHunter_Call_of_the_Wild__Hunters_Choice_BoltAction_Rifle_Pack/

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3244800/theHunter_Call_of_the_Wild__German_Shorthaired_Pointer/

In today’s post, we’ll recap everything that was announced during the show, as well as dive into some of the upcoming improvements and features you can expect in the free Winter Update.

Let’s take a look!

[h2]New Hunting Location: Salzwiesen Park[/h2]

Welcome to possibly one of the best waterfowl hunting spots in the world!

Located in Schleswig-Holstein, which sits near the border of northern Germany and Denmark, Salzwiesen Park offers a more contained biome packed with the same animal density and species diversity as our larger reserves. Here, you’ll find 15 different species, including two new birds: the plump Gadwall and the striking Ferruginous Duck, as well as two new ‘Great Ones’.

[previewyoutube=Ia4xxvu9OCk;full][/previewyoutube]

If you’re looking for a challenge, be sure to check out the Clay Shooting Range - our new gameplay feature unique to Salzwiesen Park - where you can put your accuracy skills to the ultimate test by pinpointing and pulverizing up to three flying targets at a time. Want even more of a challenge? Invite your friends and fellow hunters and compete for those sweet bragging rights as you climb the session-based leaderboard.

Salzwiesen Park also includes the versatile new GOPI 10 GRAND–the perfect shotgun for small game and clay shooting!

[h2]New Companion Dog: German Shorthaired Pointer[/h2]

Meet the newest addition to your hunting kennel!

Just as its name suggests, the German Shorthaired Pointer is designed to point you in the right direction of your desired prey. On your command, it will leap and bound its way towards all but the largest of predators, making them much easier to target.

[previewyoutube=SWXWOIep_tc;full][/previewyoutube]

Capable of pointing towards animals of all classes with the exception of harmful predators, it helps you encounter more animals and find their whereabouts quicker, delivering a more efficient hunting session. Some additional traits also bring extra utility, such as searching for a particular species after you’ve located and interacted with a clue associated with it.

Already own two dog breeds? You’re in for a treat! With the new Expert Dog feature arriving with the free update, you can customize your very own expert hunting dog by enhancing one dog with the skills of two. For example, by combining the skills of a Pointer and a Retriever, you can train your dog to skillfully flush out birds and efficiently retrieve them after you’ve taken your shot.

[h2]New Weapons: Hunters’ Choice: Bolt-Action Rifle Pack[/h2]

Get ready to take your shooting skills to new levels with the Hunters’ Choice: Bolt-Action Rifle Pack. This is the first pack to be made in collaboration with you, our incredible and supportive community.

[previewyoutube=sX51u-T9sPg;full][/previewyoutube]

Each of the three bolt-action rifles brings its own nuanced characteristics, offering owners the opportunity to engage a variety of small and large game with impressive accuracy.

[list]
[*] [b]Vallgarda .375[/b] - Your ultimate companion while hunting large and dangerous game. With the Vallgarda .375 bolt-action rifle’s accuracy and power, it’s an ideal weapon to bring with you to your hunts.
[*] [b]Johansson .450[/b] - The rugged construction and smooth operation of Johansson .450 enables it to deliver a consistent and reliable performance while offering the perfect balance between modern innovation and traditional styling.
[*] [b]Fors Elite .300[/b] - This bolt-action rifle thrives in fast-paced scenarios. Make sure to take full advantage of its rapid reloading mechanism and superior hipshot capability. Its large magazine size means extended shooting sessions are a must.
[/list]

[h2]Enjoy the Winter Update[/h2]
Check out the highlights below and keep an eye out for the full patch notes release in the future.

[list]
[*] Hunter Challenges - Say goodbye to Hunt Club Beta and take on this new challenge. Pick from a variety of daily and weekly tasks and earn in-game cash. But that's not all! Big Community Challenges are expected to make a comeback in 2025!
[*] 2 new Great Ones - What's better than one GO? Two, of course! Ring-Necked Pheasant and Red Fox will join that prestigious club in December. You will be able to find them both in Salzwiesen Park, Hirschfelden Hunting Reserve, and New England Mountains.
[*] Visual upgrades for Red Fox, European Rabbit, and Cinnamon Teal.
[*] General tweaks and improvements to the bird hunting experience.
[*] New multi-mounts.
[*] Multiple bug fixes and more!
[/list]
